cleared.check: Task 1, fix #681 (mul_mod quotient skip). The quotient-skip test was read in the crate sources of ruint 1.18.0, 1.19.0, 1.20.0, 1.20.1 and 1.21.1 from static.crates.io (sha256 of the .crate files are listed in the work directory).
cleared.result: Releases 1.18.0 to 1.20.1 do not have the fault. Their mul_mod (src/modular.rs:94-102) forms the full double-width product and runs the general division, and they do not contain rem_nxm_spare_limb. 1.21.1 contains the fix: src/algorithms/div/knuth.rs:133-136 skips the top quotient limb only when the top two normalized numerator limbs are strictly less than the divisor's. That condition is sufficient, so the skipped digit is always zero. The main-branch CHANGELOG still lists #681 under Unreleased and has no 1.21.1 section. The statement that 1.21.1 holds the fix therefore rests on the crate code, not on the changelog. When the harness copy was changed to <=, as in 1.21.0, it gave 109,148 wrong mul_mod results in 1,000,000 cases (seed 21024). The five releases gave none.

cleared.check: Task 1, change #634 (Shl and Shr by primitive integer types). The impl_shift macro and the overflowing_shl_big and wrapping_shl paths were read in all five releases.
cleared.result: In 1.18.0, 1.19.0 and 1.20.0 the operators exist only for usize, u8, u16, u32, isize, i8, i16 and i32, plus u64 and i64 on 64-bit targets (src/bits.rs:924-928 in 1.20.0). They convert with `rhs as usize`. 1.20.1 and 1.21.1 add u128 and i128 and convert with usize::try_from(rhs).unwrap_or(usize::MAX) (1.20.1 src/bits.rs:858-924). On 64-bit hosts, the change itself changes no value for any type the older releases implement. The value faults in this area come from the release-specific code listed in the next entries.

cleared.check: Task 3 finding in ruint 1.19.0: wrapping_shl, wrapping_shr and arithmetic_shr cast a usize shift amount to u32 in the 1, 2 and 4 limb fast paths (src/bits.rs:437-470 and the matching shr code). Shl and Shr by u64, i64, usize and isize go through these paths.
cleared.result: On a 64-bit host, 1.19.0 shifts by the amount mod 2^32 for amounts of 2^32 and above. It also shifts negative i64 and isize amounts by their low 32 bits. The harness found 229,169 wrong values among 1,000,000 usize-shift cases (seed 21026) and 29,657 among 1,000,000 primitive-shift cases (seed 21027), only for 64-bit amount types and only for amounts of 2^32 or more or negative 64-bit amounts. 1.20.0 fixed it with the saturating shift_amount helper (src/bits.rs:17-19). No EVM handler reaches the fault. revm-interpreter 35.0.1 to 43.0.2 and evm2 35aa3280 convert SHL, SHR and SAR amounts with a saturating usize conversion and shift only when the amount is below 256 (revm bitwise.rs shl, shr and sar; evm2 bitwise.rs:61-82). SIGNEXTEND shifts by at most 247. ruint 1.19.0 is linked by Base v1.5.6 and mega-evm v1.7.4 (MegaETH). On both networks, 2,950 SHL, SHR and SAR vectors each with amounts 2^32+k, 2^64+k and 2^128+k match the specification.

cleared.check: Task 3 finding in ruint 1.18.0 and 1.19.0: the overflow flag of overflowing_shl for amounts 64 to 255.
cleared.result: In 1.18.0 and 1.19.0 the flag is wrong in 33,418 of 1,000,000 cases (seed 21026). The shifted value is correct. This matches fix #603 of 1.20.0 in the changelog. revm and evm2 handlers use only the value (Shl<usize> calls wrapping_shl, which takes .0), so no opcode result depends on the flag. X Layer (xlayer v0.0.7, ruint 1.18.0), Base and MegaETH (1.19.0) link these releases.

cleared.check: Tasks 1 to 3, faults #701 and #704 (wrapping_from of negative integers). The macro impl_from_signed_int and support/num_bigint.rs were read in all five releases. They are byte-identical (md5 e9783126 and 02ce5067).
cleared.result: All five releases have both faults and none has a fix. Uint::wrapping_from(-v) for a primitive narrower than the Uint returns the narrow two's complement zero-extended. For example, -10i16 becomes 65526 in a U256 (src/from.rs:494-521). Every one of the 625,497 negative inputs out of 1,000,000 (seed 21029) gave that result in each release. For BigInt the result is the magnitude (src/support/num_bigint.rs:53-62). Most clients compile the num-bigint feature, according to their lockfiles. No instruction handler on the PoolManager's path calls wrapping_from, saturating_from, a signed-primitive conversion or a BigInt conversion. A search of revm-interpreter 35.0.1 to 43.0.2, evm2 35aa3280 and mega-evm v1.7.4 instructions.rs finds only U256::from of bool, u8, usize, u64 and the non-negative literal 1 or 31 (From<i32> on a positive value). Signed opcodes are built from wrapping_neg, limb XOR and wrapping_sub (revm i256.rs; evm2 i256.rs:52-62).

cleared.check: Task 2: the ruint functions that the handlers of the PoolManager's opcodes call. Sources: revm-interpreter 35.0.1, 36.0.0, 37.0.0, 37.0.3, 41.0.0, 42.0.0, 43.0.0, 43.0.1 and 43.0.2; evm2 35aa3280; mega-evm v1.7.4.
cleared.result: revm 36 to 43 arithmetic, bitwise and control files are identical, and 35.0.1 differs only in the handler signature. The handlers call wrapping_add, wrapping_mul, wrapping_sub, wrapping_div, wrapping_rem, Div, Rem, add_mod, mul_mod, pow or wrapping_pow, bit, Shl<usize>, Shr<usize>, arithmetic_shr, byte, Ord and PartialOrd (including PartialOrd<i32> in evm2 SIGNEXTEND), Eq, is_zero, BitAnd, BitOr, BitXor, Not, wrapping_neg, from_limbs, as_limbs, wrapping_to<u64>, saturating_to<u64>, TryFrom<Uint> for usize and u64, to_be_bytes and from_be_slice. Jump targets and SHL, SHR, SAR and BYTE indices use usize::try_from(..).unwrap_or(usize::MAX). Memory, return-data and CALL offsets use a raw limb check (as_usize_or_fail) that bypasses ruint. evm2 replaces that check with an AVX2 test of the upper limbs on x86. mega-evm v1.7.4 wraps the stock revm-interpreter 37.0.3 handlers (instructions.rs:3113-3263), and its own operand_as_usize is a limb check (instructions.rs:1567-1573). The harness tested every function on this list on 1,000,000 cases per group in each release, and none is faulty in any of the five. The faulty functions (narrow-amount shift fast paths in 1.19.0, the overflow flag in 1.18.0 and 1.19.0, signed wrapping_from in all) are not on the path.

cleared.check: Task 4: 24,413 eth_call vectors (seed 2102101) through the battery dispatcher. They cover SHL, SHR, SAR, BYTE and SIGNEXTEND with amounts 2^32+k, 2^33+k, 3*2^32+k, 2^63+k, 2^64+k, 2^128+k, 2^192+k and 2^64-1-k; EXP with every power of two base up to 2^63 and exponents 0 to 39, 63 to 257, 2^32, 2^64 and 2^256-1; 1,500 MULMOD and 1,500 MULDIV512 cases in the mul_mod fault shape; 1,000 ADDMOD cases near the modulus; limb-edge comparisons; and CALLDATALOAD with high-bit offsets. 28 single probes cover JUMP and JUMPI to 0x30 plus 2^32, 2^64, 2^128, 2^192 and 2^255, and MLOAD and RETURN with high-limb offsets. Each network batch is bracketed by web3_clientVersion.
cleared.result: All 21 networks returned the specified word for all 24,413 vectors. Every probe that a node answered was as specified: jumps with high limbs gave InvalidJump, and oversize offsets failed. Exceptions are limited to transport refusals. The publicnode endpoints for Ethereum and Polygon refused some probes with HTTP 403. drpc (eth.drpc.org and polygon.drpc.org, whose backend client is hidden) answered all 28 as specified. Client versions reported include reth v2.11.0-b9abbcc, base v1.5.6, xlayer v0.0.7, mega-reth v2.3.1-4499c42, tempo v1.19.1-a9d6748, op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4, conduit-op-reth v2.5.1 and world-chain v2.8.2. HyperEVM reports only 'hyperliquid evm Mainnet', so no network-side value differs from the specification.

leads.question: Run the cycle 21 ruint harness on riscv32 and MIPS64 builds of ruint 1.18.0 and 1.20.0, as linked by the Base SP1 range program (6efa756) and kona-client v1.9.0, under an emulator. usize is 32 bits on riscv32, and in 1.18.0 and 1.19.0 overflowing_shl_big casts u64 to usize.
leads.why: The EVM handlers clamp shift amounts before calling ruint, so the known truncation should be off the path. On a 32-bit target, as_usize_saturated and the jump target conversion take other branches, and the proof program decides withdrawals.

leadResults.answer: ruint 1.20.1 Shl and Shr by every primitive type give the specified result for amounts 0 to 300, 2^32, 2^64 and negative amounts. Each of the five releases got 1,000,000 primitive-shift and 1,000,000 usize-shift cases (seeds 21027 and 21026), and 1.20.1 had no mismatch. revm-interpreter 43.0.2, which nanoreth nb-20261125-2 pins, implements SHL, SHR and SAR as usize::try_from(amount).unwrap_or(MAX), checked below 256, then Shl<usize>, Shr<usize> or arithmetic_shr. The HyperEVM official endpoint matched all 24,413 new vectors and 28 probes. No public endpoint was confirmed to run nb-20261125-2: the endpoint reports only 'hyperliquid evm Mainnet'.

#701 and #704 are fixed in none of 1.18.0, 1.19.0, 1.20.0, 1.20.1 or 1.21.1, and the code is byte-identical across them. The harness confirms the wrong wrapping_from result for every negative input. #681 is in 1.21.1 by code reading (strict < in knuth.rs:133-136), although the main CHANGELOG still files it under Unreleased. No handler in revm-interpreter 35 to 43, mega-evm v1.7.4 or evm2 35aa3280 calls wrapping_from or any signed or BigInt conversion. SDIV, SMOD, SAR, SLT and SGT are built from wrapping_neg or limb XOR with wrapping_sub. SIGNEXTEND uses a positive literal. Offsets and forwarded gas use limb checks, try_from or saturating_to.

Release builds of 1.18.0 and 1.20.0, with 1.19.0, 1.20.1 and 1.21.1, ran natively on x86_64 with cargo 1.97 against Python integers. The runs covered 1,000,000 cases each for arithmetic and comparison, div_rem, pow, mul_mod, add_mod, two shift groups, conversions, signed construction and byte conversion. 1.20.0 had no mismatch. 1.18.0 showed only the overflowing_shl flag fault (#603, fixed in 1.20.0), which no handler reads.
This unit built only for x86_64. No aarch64 target or emulator is present, so the aarch64 code generation of ruint 1.21.1 and the evm2 NEON kernel are still not run natively.
